slides.say: Given: x is smaller than zero. What is ten plus four x over the absolute value of x?

So they're asking what an expression is equal to, and all we know is that x is negative. And what did we say about an expression with a letter? We're allowed to plug in a number. [short pause] So we'll start with plugging in, and then we'll do the algebra.

[short pause] Our first method, plugging in numbers. x has to be negative, so I'll take negative two. Why negative two? Before I plug in, I glance at the choices. At negative two they give fourteen, six, two and twelve, all different. So one plug-in will be enough.
Negative six would be a bad pick, by the way. Then minus x is six, and two choices would come out the same.
So four times negative two is negative eight. The absolute value of negative two is two. Negative eight over two is negative four, and ten minus four is six.
Which choice gives six at negative two? Only number two. So six, number two is our answer.
[pause] Our second method, the algebra. x is negative, so what's its absolute value? To turn a negative number positive, I take minus x. So the absolute value of x is minus x.
at: So the absolute value of x is minus x

slides.say: Now careful here. A lot of students see minus x and think it's negative. It isn't. x itself is negative, so minus x is positive.
So four x over minus x. The x's cancel, and four over minus one is negative four. Ten minus four is six.
at: So four x over minus x

slides.say: And remember this one from earlier in the course. x over its absolute value is always one or minus one. When x is negative, like negative eight over eight, it's minus one.
So the answer doesn't depend on x at all. That's why numbers three and four, with an x in them, can't be right. So six again, number two.

slides: [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
